## Summary

Per-request: profiled all 49 registered map generators round-robin with randomly chosen parameters, found the shared-primitive hotspots, and optimized them without changing generator behavior.

**Profiling.** Added `test/MapGeneratorProfileFixture.cpp` (`scons ... map-generator-profile-fixture`), a load generator that round-robins every registered generator, drawing shared controls (width/height/teams/workers) and each generator's own controls at random each attempt via the existing `GenerationRequest::randomizeControls`, and calling `GenerationService::generate` from a fresh `Game` — the same request shape the lobby produces. Ran it for 500 rounds in the background and attached macOS `sample` (1ms resolution, 180s) to it.

**Finding 1: `Torus` coordinate wrap.** `MapGeneration::floodFrom` (the 8-connected BFS in `Grid.cpp`, used from ~40 generator files as the base reachability/route/crossing primitive) accounted for **~31% of all sampled CPU time**, not because of any one generator but because it's called constantly everywhere. The cause: `Torus::x()`/`y()` (toroidal coordinate wrap) computed a double modulo (`((v % w) + w) % w`) on every one of the 8 neighbours of every visited tile, even though almost every caller offsets an already in-range coordinate by a small amount. The same per-element-modulo pattern showed up in the sliding-window scans behind `dilate`/`erode` and the box-blur/distance-transform primitives (`slideAny`, `blurLine`, `distanceLine` in `Morphology.cpp`/`Patterns.cpp`).

**Fix 1 (all in `src/map/generator/shared/`, generation-only, not reachable from live simulation):**
- `Grid.h`: `Torus::x()/y()` return the coordinate directly when it's already in `[0, w)`/`[0, h)`, falling back to the original double-remainder formula otherwise — identical result either way, just one comparison instead of two divisions in the common case.
- `Grid.cpp`: `floodFrom` hoists the wrapped row index out of the per-neighbour `dx` loop (it doesn't depend on `dx`) and skips the `(0,0)` self-neighbour, which was always a guaranteed-false check.
- `Morphology.cpp` / `Patterns.cpp`: `slideAny`, `blurLine`, `distanceLine` split their O(n) sliding-window loops into a plain-indexed middle segment and two small wrapped end segments, instead of a modulo per element throughout.

**Finding 2: the fertility kernel.** `Fertility::Field::rebuild` (`src/map/FertilityField.cpp`) also showed up, at 5-9% of sampled time. It's used at map-generation time (many generator files, and `StartQuality.cpp`, which bakes its result into `Map::Tile::fertility`), and that field is read back by `AIMaxima`'s farm planning during play and is part of the save format — so, unlike the generation-only files above, this one's output does reach live simulation, just not through any per-tick recomputation (it's a pure, deterministic, integer-only function of the water/sand masks, computed once and stored). Two loop-invariant computations were being redone per tile instead of once: `buildWrappedIndexes()` computed `offset % width`/`offset % height` inside the per-x/per-y loop despite not depending on x/y, and the correction loops in `rebuild()` looked up `xWrap[dx * width]`/`xWrap[2 * dx * width]` inside the `dy` loop despite not depending on `dy` (recomputing each of the 31 distinct values 31 times over).

**Fix 2:** pure algebraic hoists in `FertilityField.cpp` — identical values, computed once and cached instead of on every inner-loop iteration.

**Not touched further:** the AI's own farming code (`AIMaximaFarmingPolicy.cpp`/`AIMaximaFarming.cpp`) turns out to have an *independent*, separately-implemented copy of this same kernel (`AIMaxima::Farming::ExactFertilityCache`) that I did not touch — changing it would need the stronger cross-platform per-tick checksum verification this change doesn't attempt, and it wasn't a profiling hotspot in the generation-focused fixture anyway.

## Verification (behavior-preserving)

- `MapGeneratorGoldenTest <profile> --print`: all 392 golden fingerprints byte-identical before/after, and pass against the committed `macos-arm64` table (`392 golden rows compared, 0 failures`), after both commits.
- `MapGeneratorGoldenTest <profile> --sweep`: identical pass/fail pattern across 10 size/colony cells x 5 seeds x 49 generators (`0 failing combinations`), after both commits.
- `MapGeneratorGoldenTest <profile> --performance`: still reports bit-identical serialized maps, RNG state and telemetry (`PASS 49 generators`).
- `MapGeneratorDefaultsTest`: all passes, including its brute-force oracles for the flood/Chebyshev distance and the morphology distance transform.
- `test/TestsRunner`'s `FertilityFieldTest` (203 tests, all pass): exhaustively checks every tile of the fertility field against a direct O(31x31)-per-tile brute-force kernel, for both explicit paths, the adaptive path, non-power-of-two dimensions (23x17, smaller than the kernel), and hand-built sand/water edge cases.
- The profiling fixture itself, run with the same seed and round count before/after each commit: all 49 generators produced **exactly the same attempt/success/failure counts** (734/684/50) both times, meaning RNG consumption order is unchanged throughout.

## Performance

Fixture run (seed 777, 15 rounds, identical binaries/flags otherwise) — summed generation time across all 49 generators: **82.95s -> 54.94s (1.51x)** after the `Grid`/`Morphology`/`Patterns` fixes, then **-> 53.64s** after the `FertilityField` fix (a further ~2.4%, concentrated in generators that lean on fertility scoring: braided-river and islands both improved ~8.5% on that commit alone). Every generator improved or was unchanged (`uniform`, which does no flood/wrap/fertility work, is flat as expected); several improved 2x+ on the first commit (hilbert-river 2.72x, hedgerow-country 2.36x, carousel 2.32x, sierpinski-gardens 2.35x). A follow-up `sample` profile confirms `floodFrom`'s self-time share dropped from ~31% to ~18%.

## Docs

Documented the new fixture in `test/README.md`, `docs/map-generators/MAP_GENERATOR_FRAMEWORK.md`'s verification-tools list, and the map-design skill's implementation-and-verification reference.

## Test plan

- [x] `MapGeneratorGoldenTest <profile> --performance` — PASS, identical bytes/RNG/telemetry
- [x] `MapGeneratorDefaultsTest <profile>` — all PASS
- [x] `(cd test && scons -j8 && ./TestsRunner)` — 203 tests, all PASS (includes `FertilityFieldTest`'s brute-force oracle)
- [x] `MapGeneratorProfileFixture <profile> 777 15` compared before/after each commit — identical per-generator counts, 1.51x then a further ~1.024x faster
